Thanks Alice — attaching a first-pass MAP and an acceptance-test roster (attached: trial-acceptance-roster.xlsx, redwood-map-draft.pdf). Below is the short-form we propose so procurement/security can review now.

Summary of trial (4 weeks):
- Scope: Integration of Redwood hosted inference with Mediq Triage (inbound API, prefix caching enabled).
- Primary objective: Validate clinical-response recall and production latency under representative traffic.

Proposed success criteria (pass = ALL must be met):
1) Functional correctness: >= 92% recall on the curated evaluation set (50K clinical prompts) measured by Mediq evaluation scripts.
2) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end for 512-token requests <= 240ms for normal traffic; <= 350ms for burst windows (as defined in roster).
3) Stability: No more than 3 unplanned infra errors (5xx) during business hours across the trial.
4) Data controls & audit: Audit log sampling demonstrates all requests hashed and routed per the agreed retention policy.

Exit gates (immediate stop conditions):
- Any single production-grade security incident leading to data exposure.
- Sustained 95th percentile latency > 400ms for more than 12 consecutive hours.
- Functional regression: decrease in recall > 5 absolute points compared to baseline.

Acceptance-test roster (owner | test | input | pass threshold | cadence):
- Mediq Eval (Mediq) | curated clinical set (50K) | >= 92% recall | once at trial start and once at week 4
- Latency smoke (SE) | synthetic and replay traffic | 95p <= 240ms | daily during business hours
- Error surface (Infra) | production traffic sampling | < 0.5% 5xx | continuous monitoring
- Regression probe (Data) | targeted edge-case suite | no new critical failures | weekly

Owners and contacts:
- Mediq Eval owner: Alice Monroe (Mediq) — provides eval script and baseline.
- Tech integration + latency: Marcus Lin (Redwood) — will own replay and sampling.
- Acceptance coordinator: Priya Natarajan (Redwood) — single point to collect evidence & sign-off.
- Sales engineering runbook & rollback: Ben Carter (Redwood).

Proposed cutover trigger to production:
- Formal sign-off after week 4 where evidence meets all success criteria and procurement completes contract signature.

Proposed rollback signals (if any are tripped during early rollout):
- Automatic route rollback to canary variant if 95p latency exceeds threshold for 30 minutes.
- Immediate freeze and post-mortem if a stopgate condition occurs.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can Mediq confirm the evaluation set and owner by end of day Thursday?
2) Marcus & Ben — please confirm tech tests and any additional telemetry we'll need to attach to the roster.
3) Alice — procurement asked for the MAP as a two-page appendix; I'm attaching the draft.

Thanks — sending the XLSX and PDF now.

--

Priya — quick confirmation on tech items from my side so the acceptance roster is actionable:

- Latency test details: we'll use a replay harness that mirrors 1:1 request distribution for 72 hours and a synthetic stress run (90th/95th/99th). For the trial we should record both server-side inference latency and end-to-end (client->Redwood->client) numbers.
- KV/prefix cache: we recommend enabling prefix caching for the trial; note this changes throughput/latency profiles — documented in the attached XLSX.
- Telemetry needed from Mediq: sample traces (redaction applied) for 1000 representative requests and their expected outputs to seed the regression probes.
- Failure modes: define what counts as a "critical failure" (e.g., hallucination that would materially change triage outcome). I propose a three-category severity matrix in the roster.

I can own the daily latency smoke and the replay harness; Ben can run the regression probes with Mediq's eval owner.

--
Marcus Lin
Lead Infra Engineer, Integration
Redwood Inference
